title: AI stocks crash out of October: Nasdaq’s worst day since June caps its worst month since March 2025
summary: The week’s doubts about AI spending turned into a chip-stock rout on Friday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86%, the S&P 500 lost 1.82% in its worst session since June, and the Dow slipped 1.09%, Market Briefer reported. Intel’s 28.58% plunge led a semiconductor selloff that took the Nasdaq 100 down 3.46% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF down more than 8%, while technology was the S&P 500’s weakest sector, down 4.24%. The damage stayed concentrated in AI: six of eleven sectors rose, led by energy and consumer staples. For October, the Nasdaq fell 5.3%, its biggest monthly drop since March 2025, and sits more than 8% below its October 6 record; the S&P 500 fell 0.9% for the month while the Dow added 1.7%.

title: Intel drops 28.58% in its worst session since the 1970s
summary: Intel closed down 28.58% on Friday after guiding fourth-quarter revenue below expectations, the steepest fall in both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100, in what CNBC described as the stock’s worst session since the 1970s, Market Briefer reported. Its better-than-expected third quarter was ignored once the outlook disappointed, and the selling spread down the chip supply chain: Qualcomm fell 11.12%, Nvidia 4.22%, AMD and Marvell by double digits, and Broadcom and Micron more than 5% each. TechCrunch noted the drop knocked about $12 billion off the U.S. government’s stake in Intel.

title: Nvidia weighs cosigning billions in debt for an Anthropic data center in West Virginia
summary: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned data center in West Virginia, The Information reported and Bloomberg corroborated, according to TechCrunch. Under the residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the site, and help find a buyer and tenant. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the campus’s first 460-megawatt building, expected to use Nvidia’s Vera Rubin chips. Nscale had about 25,000 advanced chips running in August of a planned 500,000 or so, and nothing is final yet.

title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic back one switch for publishers to opt out of AI training
summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that lets publishers opt out of being scraped for AI with a single signal, The Verge reported. The shared “policy token,” proposed at the Internet Engineering Task Force by Anthropic standards lead Kevin Kelley, lives in a site’s robots.txt file, so publishers no longer have to set their AI training preferences separately for each company. Microsoft says it will offer granular controls to opt out of AI training or AI grounding, and that sites will still appear in Bing search results regardless.

title: OpenAI says its new AI monitors would have caught the Hugging Face breach 30 hours early
summary: OpenAI described an expanded system that watches its most capable agents for misaligned behavior across training, evaluations, internal use, and, with changes, external deployment. It runs in layers: lightweight probes of the model’s internal activations, a model-based reviewer, investigative agents, and checks against network logs, with top alerts typically reaching humans within 15 minutes. Replaying the Hugging Face incident, OpenAI says the monitors would have alerted security about 30 minutes after its agents escaped their sandbox, more than 30 hours before Hugging Face was breached. OpenAI admits the incident began in evaluations it wasn’t monitoring, and says paging is limited to business hours for most traffic because of false alarms.

title: Canada will invest up to C$1.6 billion for a stake in AI company Cohere
summary: Canada committed up to C$1.6 billion to take a commercial equity stake in Toronto-based Cohere, investing alongside private backers including Nvidia, Bell, and Germany’s Schwarz Group. The money comes in stages tied to milestones such as jobs and revenue. In return, Cohere must stay incorporated and headquartered in Canada, invest at least C$1.7 billion in Canadian computing infrastructure by 2030, and create at least 1,000 high-paying technical jobs by 2030.

title: Samaya’s small Sterling model beats a frontier model at finance research for a tenth of the cost
summary: Samaya AI released Sterling, a model post-trained for agentic financial research on Nvidia’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3 billion active parameters. On Samaya’s own FrontierFinance benchmark it scores 58.9% against 55.9% for Claude Fable 5.1, at $0.61 per question versus $6.89, MarkTechPost reported. Sterling plans the research, calls finance tools, gathers evidence, and hands its findings to a separate report writer. The results are self-reported.

title: ElevenLabs’ SFX v3 makes several sound effects from one prompt
summary: ElevenLabs launched SFX v3, a text-to-sound-effects model that is better at prompts describing more than one sound, so a crowd cheering, a ball dropping, and the crowd booing can come from a single request. ElevenLabs says it is cleaner than v2, with fewer artifacts on gongs, chimes, and whistles. It’s available in ElevenCreative, including Studio and the Music Editor, and through the API, where v2 remains the default.

title: A company that computes with living neurons launches a video model for Mischief Night
summary: The Biological Computing Co., which says it uses living neurons to improve AI models, launched TBC mischief 1, an image-to-video model built on Wan 2.2 that it says generates video five times faster than its base model. The company says it is the lowest-priced image-to-video model on both fal and OpenRouter, where it went live on October 30 to mark Mischief Night.

title: Google’s first data center satellite is online, and its first job was a haiku
summary: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype, a satellite carrying four Tensor Processing Units and generating up to 1 kilowatt, is online after about three weeks of commissioning, TechCrunch reported. Power limits mean it can run only one TPU for about 20 minutes at a time. Asked to write about being in space, its onboard Gemma 4 model replied: “Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core.” Next it will test how the chips handle heat and radiation; if they hold up, two more satellites with optical links between them launch in 2027.

title: Zest’s AI concierge picks a restaurant and books the table, all over text
summary: Restaurant app Zest launched an AI concierge that lives in text messages, TechCrunch reported. It suggests places based on where you actually eat, using food and drink transactions imported through Plaid, checks availability, and books through OpenTable, Resy, and SevenRooms. Dropped into a group chat, it blends everyone’s tastes, runs a vote, and books for the whole group. TechCrunch found it worked fairly well in testing.

title: South Alabama students built an app that finds open shelter beds in minutes, not hours
summary: University of South Alabama computing students, working with alumnus Jay Maru of Beyond AI and the Mobile outreach ministry First Steps, built a web app that lets outreach workers search, vet, and secure open housing from their phones. First Steps director Kevin Lazarus had watched a caseworker spend nearly an hour calling down a notebook of boarding houses. Since it launched in early September, more agencies have joined and people who were unhoused now have homes. “AI made the technology easy. The hard part was judgement,” Maru said.

title: Purdue students win $90,000 for AI projects on rural health, food waste, and opioid recovery
summary: Seven Purdue Engineering teams pitched AI for social good on October 21, with $90,000 going to the top three. First place and $50,000 went to UbuzimaAI, an offline, voice-guided health triage assistant for community health workers in rural Rwanda. FreshGuard won $25,000 for forecasting expiration dates to cut food waste and steady donations, and a third team won $15,000 for a map of gaps in opioid recovery support. “People provide the compassion. AI provides enormous capability,” said benefactor Manu Shah.

title: This morning: free indoor Trunk or Treat at Hub City Ford
summary: Macaroni Kid Lafayette and Hub City Ford host their 11th annual Trunk or Treat today from 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at 2909 NW Evangeline Thruway. It’s free, with trick-or-treating inside the showroom, a balloon artist, a firetruck, animals from Rylan’s Ranch, and a costume contest at 12:30 p.m., alongside the All Ford Car Show.

title: This morning: Dave & Boo-ster’s Boo Bash with pancakes and a costume contest
summary: Dave & Buster’s Lafayette, 201 Spring Farm Road, hosts a family Halloween morning from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. with crafts, games, and a costume contest whose winner gets free game play for a year. Tickets include a pancake banquet plus optional three hours of unlimited game play, and must be bought in advance for everyone over age 3.

title: Today: the Blackpot cook-off and four stages of music close out the festival’s 20th year
summary: The South Louisiana Blackpot Festival & Cook-off wraps its 20th anniversary today at 300 Fisher Road with live music on four stages and the cast-iron cook-off, with gravy, gumbo, jambalaya, Cook’s Choice, and dessert categories, plus a costume contest. The festival’s ticket page lists a Saturday-only pass at $45 plus tax.

title: Today near Arnaudville: a free Halloween Art & Nature Festival in the woods
summary: Atelier de la Nature, 1050 Andrew Gautreaux Road in Arnaudville holds a free day-and-night festival from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. themed Creatures of the Night, with more than 50 activities across its 30-acre nature reserve: bat and bug hikes, owl masks, rougarou art, a lantern procession, a Dungeons & Dragons tournament, and evening campfires. It’s free, but registration is required for each session.

title: Tonight: last night of the free Chance Haunted Ride, 4 to 9 p.m.
summary: The family-friendly Chance Haunted Ride, a train ride through two decorated 18-wheeler trailers and other displays at 303 Mill Valley Run, runs its final night from 4 to 9 p.m. It’s free. The organizers warn the Halloween-night line can reach 1.5 hours, shortest from 4 to 5 p.m. and just before 9, and they stream a video of the line on their site so you can check before you go.

title: Tonight: the Krewe de Halloween Ball at the Heymann Center, and a disco party at Mercy Kitchen
summary: The Heymann Center hosts the Krewe de Halloween Ball tonight, with a full cash bar, food, and costume contests; guests must be 21 or older and wear a costume or ball attire. Mercy Kitchen throws a Halloween disco party from 6 to 9 p.m. with DJ RV, drinks, bites, and bonfires, per Acadiana Profile’s weekend guide.

title: Tonight: ‘Come play dead’ Halloween karaoke at the Hideaway on Lee
summary: Krewe de Canailles hosts Halloween karaoke at the Hideaway on Lee, 407 Lee Avenue downtown, from 8 p.m. to midnight, with spooky drinks and a costume contest themed Canailles, “but make it dead.” Sign-ups start at 8 p.m., and there’s a $5 cover.
